notice: Fictional scenarios for education only. Not for real-patient care, diagnosis, treatment, prescribing, or procedural decision-making.

patient_cases.name: Post-operative ward check
patient_cases.presentation: A fictional adult is recovering after an uncomplicated operation. Practise a structured bedside review and recognise that one set of observations is not the whole clinical picture.
observations: Introduce yourself, confirm the simulated patient identity and explain what you are checking.
Assess general appearance, breathing effort, circulation and level of consciousness.
Review observations as a trend rather than interpreting a single number in isolation.
Ask about pain, nausea, fluids, urine output and any new symptoms.
Summarise your findings and state when you would ask the supervising clinician to review.
patient_cases.debrief: A reassuring observation set does not exclude every complication. Context, baseline observations, procedure, medicines, trends and the patient's concerns matter.

patient_cases.name: Respiratory deterioration
patient_cases.presentation: A fictional patient has increasing breathlessness and cough. Your task is to assess immediate stability, interpret observations, and organise a focused handover. This is a teaching case, not a triage tool.
observations: Look for increased work of breathing and ability to speak.
Review respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, heart rate, blood pressure, temperature and consciousness together.
Use an airway–breathing–circulation–disability–exposure structure under supervision.
Collect relevant history and focused examination findings without delaying escalation for instability.
Give a concise handover with situation, background, assessment, and recommendation.
patient_cases.debrief: Marked respiratory distress or worsening observations require urgent clinical assessment in real life. The simulator cannot diagnose the cause or safely recommend oxygen or medication settings.

patient_cases.name: Fever with possible infection
patient_cases.presentation: A fictional adult has fever, tachycardia and malaise. Practise recognising possible deterioration, identifying information needed, and communicating concern promptly.
observations: Assess airway, breathing, circulation and mental status immediately in the simulated scenario.
Review perfusion, blood pressure, pulse, respiratory rate, temperature, oxygen saturation and urine-output history.
Gather recent infection history, medicines, allergies, comorbidities and relevant exposure history.
Discuss the purpose and limitations of appropriately collected cultures and other tests with a supervisor.
Escalate concern and communicate the observed changes clearly; do not use this exercise to make real treatment decisions.
patient_cases.debrief: This is an educational deterioration scenario. Sepsis cannot be confirmed or excluded from a single sign or this mock score. Real suspected sepsis requires immediate professional assessment and local protocols.

patient_cases.name: Post-operative bleeding concern
patient_cases.presentation: A fictional post-operative patient becomes pale and tachycardic, with a falling blood pressure trend. Practise recognising a concerning pattern and escalating to the clinical team.
observations: Recognise that the combination of tachycardia and falling blood pressure can be concerning in context.
Check the simulated patient, monitor quality, recent trend and relevant post-operative background.
Use a structured ABCDE approach and summon the appropriate supervising/emergency team in the scenario.
Communicate observations and the time course; do not delay escalation to complete a checklist.
Reflect on why trends and context are important.
patient_cases.debrief: This case represents a potentially time-critical deterioration pattern. In real clinical practice, follow emergency escalation procedures immediately; the tool does not recommend treatments.

organ_systems.name: Heart & circulation
organ_systems.focus: Heart, great vessels, coronary circulation and perfusion
organ_systems.concept: Cardiac output depends on heart rate and stroke volume. Arterial pressure also reflects vascular resistance and circulating volume.
organ_systems.caseLink: Look at the pulse waveform and blood-pressure trend together; do not assume the monitor alone explains the cause.

organ_systems.name: Lungs & airway
organ_systems.focus: Upper airway, lungs, alveoli and respiratory muscles
organ_systems.concept: Gas exchange depends on ventilation, perfusion, diffusion and haemoglobin-mediated transport.
organ_systems.caseLink: Respiratory rate, work of breathing, oxygen saturation and clinical appearance are complementary rather than interchangeable.

organ_systems.name: Brain & nervous system
organ_systems.focus: Brain, spinal cord, peripheral nerves and consciousness
organ_systems.concept: Neural function depends on electrical signalling, synaptic communication and adequate oxygen/glucose delivery.
organ_systems.caseLink: A change in consciousness is important and should be interpreted with the rest of the assessment.

organ_systems.name: Kidneys & fluid balance
organ_systems.focus: Kidneys, nephron, bladder and fluid regulation
organ_systems.concept: The kidneys regulate water, electrolytes, acid–base balance and excretion; urine output is one part of the wider picture.
organ_systems.caseLink: Review intake/output trends and relevant labs with supervision; one number is not a diagnosis.

organ_systems.name: Liver & metabolism
organ_systems.focus: Liver, portal circulation and hepatobiliary system
organ_systems.concept: The liver participates in nutrient processing, protein synthesis, bile production and metabolism of many substances.
organ_systems.caseLink: Liver assessment requires history, examination and a pattern of laboratory results rather than a single score.

organ_systems.name: GI tract & pancreas
organ_systems.focus: Stomach, intestines, pancreas and biliary system
organ_systems.concept: Digestion, absorption, motility and endocrine secretion are coordinated by neural and hormonal signalling.
organ_systems.caseLink: Symptoms, hydration, abdominal findings and biochemical results must be integrated.

organ_systems.name: Blood & immune system
organ_systems.focus: Blood cells, bone marrow, immune tissues and lymphatics
organ_systems.concept: Blood transports gases and nutrients; immune pathways respond to pathogens and tissue injury.
organ_systems.caseLink: A blood count or inflammatory marker supports a clinical assessment but does not independently establish a diagnosis.

organ_systems.name: Endocrine system
organ_systems.focus: Pituitary, thyroid, adrenals, pancreas and gonads
organ_systems.concept: Hormone axes use feedback loops to regulate metabolism, stress responses, growth and reproduction.
organ_systems.caseLink: Interpret endocrine labs with symptoms, timing, medication and the appropriate reference range.

organ_systems.name: Skin & musculoskeletal
organ_systems.focus: Skin, muscles, bones, joints and soft tissues
organ_systems.concept: Skin contributes to barrier function and thermoregulation; musculoskeletal tissues support movement and protect organs.
organ_systems.caseLink: Inspect the whole clinical context and avoid anchoring on one visible feature.

organ_systems.name: Reproductive system
organ_systems.concept: Reproductive function depends on anatomy, endocrine feedback, age and individual physiology.
organ_systems.caseLink: Use respectful communication, consent, privacy and appropriate supervision in clinical scenarios.

microbiology_tests.name: Gram stain
microbiology_tests.specimen: Appropriate specimen for the clinical question (for example, a validated clinical sample)
microbiology_tests.principle: Differential staining reflects cell-envelope properties; Gram-positive organisms commonly retain crystal violet and appear purple, while Gram-negative organisms are counterstained pink/red.
microbiology_tests.learning_task: Choose a teaching interpretation for purple cocci in clusters.
options: Suggests staphylococcal morphology; identification needs confirmatory testing
Proves a specific species without further tests
Rules out infection
microbiology_tests.explanation: Gram reaction and morphology narrow possibilities but do not establish species or susceptibility. Interpret the result with specimen quality and the clinical context.
microbiology_tests.limitations: Mixed flora, staining quality, prior antibiotics and specimen source can affect interpretation.

microbiology_tests.name: Culture and colony morphology
microbiology_tests.specimen: A properly collected specimen selected for the suspected infection and laboratory protocol
microbiology_tests.principle: Viable organisms may grow on appropriate media; colony appearance is a clue, not a stand-alone identification.
microbiology_tests.learning_task: What is the safest interpretation of an unusual colony appearance?
options: Use it as a clue and continue validated identification/workflow
Name the organism from colour alone
Assume it is always contamination
microbiology_tests.explanation: Colony morphology is presumptive. Identification may require validated biochemical, mass-spectrometry or molecular methods, with appropriate quality control.
microbiology_tests.limitations: Media, incubation conditions, mixed growth and contamination affect results. Real bench work requires trained staff and laboratory SOPs.

microbiology_tests.name: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing
microbiology_tests.specimen: A pure, correctly identified isolate selected according to the laboratory's approved workflow
microbiology_tests.principle: Standardised methods estimate how an organism responds to selected antimicrobial agents; interpretation uses current standards and quality control.
microbiology_tests.learning_task: What is required before interpreting a susceptibility result?
options: A validated method, quality control and current interpretive standard
Only the size of any zone without method or standard
The patient's symptoms alone
microbiology_tests.explanation: A result must be generated and interpreted using validated methods and the applicable current standards; clinical relevance depends on site, patient factors and stewardship guidance.
microbiology_tests.limitations: Do not infer treatment choices from this exercise. Laboratory standards and breakpoints are updated and vary by organism/drug.

microbiology_tests.name: Acid-fast stain
microbiology_tests.specimen: A clinical specimen selected by a qualified service when acid-fast organisms are suspected
microbiology_tests.principle: Acid-fast staining exploits a lipid-rich cell envelope; microscopy is a screening clue and does not alone confirm or exclude tuberculosis.
microbiology_tests.learning_task: What can a positive acid-fast smear establish by itself?
options: Acid-fast organisms are seen; further validated tests and clinical assessment are needed
It definitively identifies the organism and drug resistance
It proves every respiratory symptom is tuberculosis
microbiology_tests.explanation: Smear microscopy has limitations and cannot confirm species or drug susceptibility. Molecular tests, culture and public-health pathways may be needed according to guidance.
microbiology_tests.limitations: Sensitivity depends on specimen quality and organism burden; follow biosafety procedures and official laboratory protocols.

microbiology_tests.name: KOH microscopy
microbiology_tests.specimen: A suitable skin, hair, nail or other specimen collected by trained personnel
microbiology_tests.principle: Potassium hydroxide clears keratinous material to help visualise fungal elements in selected specimens.
microbiology_tests.learning_task: What does seeing fungal elements on microscopy mean?
options: Supports a fungal cause but must be correlated with specimen, morphology and context
Always identifies the species and the ideal treatment
Excludes every other diagnosis
microbiology_tests.explanation: KOH microscopy can support recognition of fungal structures, but its sensitivity depends on sampling and interpretation; culture or other tests may be needed.
microbiology_tests.limitations: False negatives can occur with poor sampling or low organism burden. This is a virtual interpretation exercise, not a bench protocol.

microbiology_tests.name: Blood culture workflow
microbiology_tests.specimen: Blood collected by trained personnel using the institution's approved collection process
microbiology_tests.principle: Cultures are used to detect bloodstream infection; collection quality, adequate sampling and timing are important.
microbiology_tests.learning_task: What is a core pre-analytical priority?
options: Correct patient/specimen identification and aseptic collection under local SOPs
Reuse a labelled specimen container for another patient
Delay urgent clinical escalation until results return
microbiology_tests.explanation: Correct identification, collection technique, transport and communication of critical results are central. Cultures take time and cannot replace immediate care for an unstable patient.
microbiology_tests.limitations: False positives and negatives occur; results must be interpreted clinically and with microbiology advice.

microbiology_tests.name: Urinalysis
microbiology_tests.specimen: A correctly collected urine specimen appropriate to the clinical question
microbiology_tests.principle: Dipsticks assess selected chemical properties; microscopy and culture may add information depending on the situation.
microbiology_tests.learning_task: Which is the best way to interpret leukocyte esterase or nitrite?
options: As supportive findings interpreted with symptoms, collection quality and other results
As proof of urinary infection in every patient
As a direct measure of renal filtration
microbiology_tests.explanation: Urinalysis findings are not definitive in isolation; contamination, asymptomatic bacteriuria and organism characteristics affect interpretation.
microbiology_tests.limitations: Reference ranges and follow-up depend on patient group and clinical context; seek appropriate guidance.

microbiology_tests.name: ELISA / immunoassay
microbiology_tests.specimen: The validated specimen type for the specific assay
microbiology_tests.principle: Antigen–antibody binding with an enzyme-linked detection system produces a measurable signal.
microbiology_tests.learning_task: What does an assay result need before clinical interpretation?
options: The assay's validated cut-off, controls, pre-test context and confirmatory pathway if applicable
A colour change viewed without controls
Assuming all kits detect every strain/variant equally
microbiology_tests.explanation: Controls, assay performance, cut-offs and the target analyte matter. Positive and negative predictive values also depend on context and prevalence.
microbiology_tests.limitations: Assays differ. Follow current manufacturer instructions, laboratory validation and the relevant diagnostic guideline.

microbiology_tests.name: PCR / nucleic-acid test
microbiology_tests.specimen: The assay-specific validated specimen collected and transported correctly
microbiology_tests.principle: Nucleic-acid amplification detects a selected genetic target.
microbiology_tests.learning_task: What is an important limitation of a positive PCR result?
options: It detects the target nucleic acid but may not by itself prove viable organism or active disease
It always proves viable organisms and infectiousness
It gives antimicrobial susceptibility for every organism
microbiology_tests.explanation: Molecular assays are target-specific; results require assessment of sample, timing, assay limitations and clinical context. Resistance testing is only available when the assay targets relevant markers.
microbiology_tests.limitations: Contamination, timing, target variation and residual nucleic acid may affect interpretation.

microbiology_tests.name: Peripheral blood film
microbiology_tests.specimen: A correctly collected blood sample prepared and reviewed by trained personnel
microbiology_tests.principle: Cell morphology may reveal patterns involving red cells, white cells and platelets.
microbiology_tests.learning_task: What is appropriate when an abnormal cell pattern is noticed?
options: Describe the morphology and correlate with blood count, context and expert review
Make a final diagnosis from one field alone
Ignore sample quality and artefacts
microbiology_tests.explanation: Blood films are interpreted with counts, indices, history and sometimes additional tests. Morphology is a powerful clue but not a complete diagnosis.
microbiology_tests.limitations: Preparation artefacts, sampling, observer experience and clinical context matter.

items: Confirm the simulated patient's identity using the approved identifiers.
Verify planned procedure, site/side and relevant documentation.
Confirm consent, allergies and relevant risks are documented.
Review airway, monitoring, equipment and anticipated concerns with the supervising team.
Pause for the whole team to introduce roles and agree the patient/procedure/site.
Confirm relevant imaging, blood availability or special equipment if applicable.
Invite concerns from any team member and resolve them before proceeding.
Use the local checklist; do not substitute this educational list for institutional policy.
Perform surgical hand antisepsis according to the local approved protocol.
Use appropriate sterile gowning/gloving under supervision and maintain the sterile field.
Identify breaks in sterility and communicate them immediately.
Confirm skin preparation, draping and equipment checks according to local policy.
Maintain clear communication and closed-loop confirmation for key requests.
Complete instrument, needle and swab counts at the required stages according to policy.
Label and communicate any specimens correctly using the required process.
Escalate equipment problems, unexpected findings or safety concerns promptly.
Confirm the procedure performed and any specimens that require tracking.
Confirm counts, equipment concerns and post-operative plans according to the team checklist.
Provide a structured handover, including airway, breathing, circulation, pain, fluids and concerns.
Document learning points and receive supervisor feedback.

diagnostic_panels.name: Complete blood count
diagnostic_panels.context: Fictional teaching panel; units and reference intervals are illustrative and vary by laboratory.
diagnostic_panels.question: Which statement is most defensible?
options: The panel shows anaemia and leukocytosis; causes require clinical context and further assessment
This combination proves one specific disease
Normal platelets exclude serious illness
diagnostic_panels.explanation: A CBC describes cell counts, not a final diagnosis. Morphology, indices, trend, symptoms and other tests may be needed.

diagnostic_panels.name: Arterial blood gas
diagnostic_panels.context: Fictional sample for acid–base practice; real samples require correct collection and prompt validated analysis.
diagnostic_panels.question: What is the primary acid–base pattern?
options: Respiratory acidosis pattern; assess compensation, oxygenation and clinical context
Primary respiratory alkalosis
Primary metabolic alkalosis
diagnostic_panels.explanation: Low pH with raised PaCO₂ supports a respiratory acidosis pattern. Mixed disorders, timing, oxygenation and clinical state matter; do not make treatment decisions from this exercise.

diagnostic_panels.name: Renal and electrolyte panel
diagnostic_panels.context: Fictional results using illustrative reference intervals.
diagnostic_panels.question: What should a learner notice first?
options: Renal-function and electrolyte abnormalities that need prompt clinical interpretation in context
This proves chronic kidney disease without baseline or duration
A single panel defines the cause and safest treatment
diagnostic_panels.explanation: The pattern raises concern for renal dysfunction and electrolyte disturbance but does not establish cause or chronicity. Real abnormalities, especially potassium disturbance, need professional assessment using local pathways.

diagnostic_panels.name: Liver biochemistry
diagnostic_panels.context: Fictional result pattern; the laboratory's reference ranges and patient context matter.
diagnostic_panels.question: Which is the best first interpretation?
options: A predominantly hepatocellular enzyme pattern with raised bilirubin needs context and further assessment
This alone proves a single viral cause
Normal ALP excludes all hepatobiliary disease
diagnostic_panels.explanation: ALT-predominant elevation can suggest hepatocellular injury, but interpretation depends on AST, ALP, bilirubin fractions, medication/exposure history and clinical review.

diagnostic_panels.name: Cardiac markers
diagnostic_panels.context: Fictional result pattern. Do not use a single marker to assess real chest pain.
diagnostic_panels.question: What is the safest academic interpretation?
options: Myocardial injury is possible; diagnosis requires symptoms, ECG, serial change and clinical assessment
A single elevated result alone proves plaque rupture in every case
A missing ECG means cardiac disease is excluded
diagnostic_panels.explanation: Troponin elevation indicates myocardial injury in the appropriate assay context but is not specific to one cause. Real chest pain or deterioration needs urgent professional evaluation.

diagnostic_panels.name: Urinalysis
diagnostic_panels.context: Fictional dipstick results for interpretation practice.
diagnostic_panels.question: How should the findings be used?
options: Combine symptoms, collection quality and possible microscopy/culture when indicated
Treat a positive leukocyte esterase as definitive proof in every case
Use it as a direct measurement of glomerular filtration
diagnostic_panels.explanation: Dipstick findings support but do not replace clinical assessment. Contamination and asymptomatic findings can mislead, and negative nitrite does not exclude a urinary infection.
